title: Binary search
short: Find a value in a sorted list by halving it each step.
what: If a list is sorted, look at the middle. If your target is bigger, throw away the left half; if smaller, throw away the right half. Each step halves what is left, so even a million items take about 20 looks.
analogy: Guessing a number from 1 to 100 when someone says higher or lower. Start at 50 and you never need more than 7 guesses.

frames.label: find 23
frames.say: The list is sorted. We want 23. lo and hi mark the part that could still hold it: everything.

frames.label: find 23
frames.say: 16 is smaller than 23, so 23 must be to the right. Move lo to 5. Half the list is gone.

frames.label: find 23
frames.say: mid = (5 + 9) // 2 = 7. The value is 56, too big.

frames.label: find 23
frames.say: 56 is bigger than 23, so drop the right side: hi = 6. Two cells left.

frames.label: find 23
frames.say: mid = 5 holds 23. Found it in 3 looks instead of 6.

when: Find the first or last position of something
Find the smallest value that works (search on the answer)
watch: It only works on sorted data.
Use lo <= hi in the loop, and move with mid + 1 and mid - 1, or it can loop forever.
Python has it built in: bisect.bisect_left(nums, target).
